operations.name: projects.list
operations.summary: List the projects in your organisation.

live.description: False until a release is live.

operations.name: projects.get
operations.summary: Show one project and whether a release is live.

live.description: False until a release is live.

operations.name: projects.connectInfo
operations.summary: Where the project is served: the MCP URL, the REST base and dataset URLs, and the client contract.

operations.name: projects.create
operations.summary: Create a project: one ClickHouse connection, one live data model, its own URLs.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; part of every URL, so it never changes.

live.description: False until a release is live.

operations.name: projects.rename
operations.summary: Change a project's display name; its slug and URLs stay the same.

live.description: False until a release is live.

operations.name: releases.status
operations.summary: Show what is live: the current version and revision.

currentRevision.description: Pass as expectedRevision to roll back or publish.

operations.name: releases.list
operations.summary: List published versions, newest first.

operations.name: releases.get
operations.summary: Show one published version and its data model.

operations.name: releases.rollback
operations.summary: Make an earlier published version live again. The project's owner follows it: rolling back to a version built in Cloud makes the model editable in Cloud again, and to one deployed from code makes it managed in code.

operations.name: drafts.list
operations.summary: List the project's drafts and whether each is ready to publish.

stale.description: True when something else was published since this draft began.

operations.name: drafts.open
operations.summary: Open your working draft (created on first use, with the ClickHouse schema discovered) or a named draft, and see what it holds.

draft.description: A draft id; omit for your own working draft.

identity.description: The draft's content identity; drafts.save checks it hasn't changed.

stage.description: setup until the project's first publish, then draft.

setupAnswers.description: What the user said at setup, saved with drafts_setup; resume from here.

operations.name: drafts.save
operations.summary: Save the draft as a staging release after its publish gates pass. Nothing goes live; publishing is drafts.promote.

expectedIdentity.description: From drafts.open; refuses if the draft changed since. Omit to save it as it is.

operations.name: drafts.review
operations.summary: Review a saved draft before publishing: what changes against production, breaking changes, held measures and checks.

operations.name: drafts.checks
operations.summary: Run Cloud's number checks on a code draft's saved release.

rerun.description: Run again even when a result is stored.

operations.name: drafts.promote
operations.summary: Publish a draft's saved release to production.

expectedRevision.description: The live revision, or null for a first publish.

takeOwnership.description: Code drafts over a model built in Cloud: true only after the user agreed the project is then managed in code.

operations.name: drafts.get
operations.summary: Read a draft: its model, revision, whether Production moved since it was based, its saved release and its publish gates.

operations.name: drafts.rename
operations.summary: Rename a draft. Its id and staging URL stay the same.

operations.name: drafts.delete
operations.summary: Delete a draft and its staging URL for good. Only its creator can, unless you manage the organisation.

operations.name: drafts.archived
operations.summary: Read an archived draft: the release it published and whether it can be reopened against current Production.

operations.name: drafts.reopen
operations.summary: Reopen an archived draft as a working draft, from the release you read.

operations.name: drafts.impact
operations.summary: Who a saved draft affects: which apps and customers called the datasets, measures and fields it changes or removes, recently.

operations.name: drafts.evidence
operations.summary: Read a draft's evidence ledger: what discovery found, the checks run, the user's decisions and confirmations, each with its confidence, status and what it applies to. Proof stays with the customer, and sample values the sample policy withholds are cut out and marked.

revision.description: null for a draft with no working model.

hasProof.description: Measured proof exists; it stays with the customer.

withheld.description: What was left out of this entry under the sample policy.

omitted.description: Entries of a kind not yet cleared for the model, left out entirely.

operations.name: drafts.replay
operations.summary: Replay a few of the last week's queries on the datasets a saved draft changes, against Production and the draft, and say whether each answer is the same. Only statuses, row counts and outcomes are returned, never rows.

releaseIdentity.description: The saved release you reviewed (releaseIdentity from drafts_impact).

publishedRevision.description: The Production it was compared with (publishedRevision from drafts_impact).

status.description: The HTTP status; null when it didn't run.
The HTTP status; null when it didn't run.

outcome.description: truncated: a full page may be any subset of the result, so not compared.

stopped.description: The time limit stopped the replay early.

operations.name: drafts.update
operations.summary: When Production moved since a draft was based, show the merge onto current Production: what merges cleanly and each conflict to choose.

operations.name: drafts.applyUpdate
operations.summary: Merge a draft onto current Production with the user's choice for each conflict (keep the draft's or Production's). Preview first; apply once every conflict is chosen.

resolutions.description: Each conflict's key from drafts_update, and which side the user chose.

operations.name: drafts.refreshBase
operations.summary: For a code draft whose base Production moved: acknowledge that publishing it will replace current Production as it is, dropping the changes made there since. Nothing is merged.

operations.name: drafts.setup
operations.summary: Save what the user said about the project on a draft: what it's for, who it serves, the tables to model, priority metrics and one number they trust.

answers.description: The user's own statements; tables must be names drafts_open listed.

operations.name: drafts.findings
operations.summary: List what discovery found that changes numbers (internal rows, mixed units, versioned rows, grain, customer scope…), each with the question to ask the user and the measures it affects.

issues.description: Answer each with drafts_answer, passing its id and token.

operations.name: drafts.answer
operations.summary: Record the user's answers to findings: approve the proposed default, reject it (remove, or their own alternative), or decide later. Each answer becomes the member's decision in the draft's evidence ledger and can release held measures, so ask the user first.

text.description: The user's alternative, in their words.

operations.name: drafts.runStatus
operations.summary: Read the progress of the draft's background checks (grain, column meaning, measures, joins, query history, the trusted number).

operations.name: drafts.run
operations.summary: Start, resume or cancel the draft's background checks against ClickHouse. They run in batches; poll drafts_run_status, then read drafts_findings.

operations.name: customerScope.list
operations.summary: List each live dataset's customer scope, and the ones flagged for exposing a customer column without being scoped by it.

live.description: false until the project has a published release.

scoped.description: Each request names a customer and sees only its rows.

candidate.description: A customer-looking column the dataset exposes without being scoped by it.

shared.description: A member confirmed it is the same for every customer.

unsettled.description: Flagged datasets nobody has settled yet.

operations.name: customerScope.confirmShared
operations.summary: Record that a flagged dataset is the same for every customer, so it stays unscoped on purpose. Only the user can decide this.

live.description: false until the project has a published release.

scoped.description: Each request names a customer and sees only its rows.

candidate.description: A customer-looking column the dataset exposes without being scoped by it.

shared.description: A member confirmed it is the same for every customer.

unsettled.description: Flagged datasets nobody has settled yet.

operations.name: samplePolicy.get
operations.summary: Read which columns' sample values the assistant may see: all, only those not detected as sensitive, or none, with per-column overrides.

operations.name: samplePolicy.set
operations.summary: Set which columns' sample values the assistant may see.

operations.name: connections.get
operations.summary: Show the project's ClickHouse connection (never the password).

database.description: The default database: bare dataset sources read it.

operations.name: connections.save
operations.summary: Test and save the project's ClickHouse connection; once a release is live, databases can only be added.

database.description: The default database: bare dataset sources read it.

operations.name: connections.link
operations.summary: Get a one-time link for the user to enter the project's ClickHouse connection in the dashboard, so the password never passes through chat. It works for the user who asked, signed in, once, for 15 minutes; then check it with connections.test.

url.description: Give this to the user to open; never ask for the password instead.

operations.name: connections.test
operations.summary: Check the saved connection now: reachable, the user accepted, and what hypequery needs granted.

operations.name: connections.queryHistory
operations.summary: Show whether onboarding may read ClickHouse query history, and which accounts are technical.

operations.name: connections.setQueryHistory
operations.summary: Allow or stop onboarding reading ClickHouse query history (shapes only, never literals).

operations.name: logs.query
operations.summary: Search the project's request history (7 days): who queried what, how long it took, and what failed.

q.description: Search request paths and failure codes.

operations.name: logs.get
operations.summary: Explain one answer by its request ID: the customer, end user (as a pseudonym), dataset, release and version, semantic query, timing and row count.

requestId.description: The x-hypequery-request-id header of a REST answer, or com.hypequery/requestId in an MCP result's _meta.

operations.name: usage.get
operations.summary: Show this month's queries by day and transport, per customer, and embedded chat usage.

operations.name: audit.list
operations.summary: List the organisation's audit log: publishes, rollbacks, members, keys and connection changes.

operations.name: tenants.list
operations.summary: List the project's customers (tenants) and whether each is enabled.

operations.name: tenants.create
operations.summary: Register a customer by the id your app uses for it, with a display name.

tenantKey.description: Your app's id for the customer.

operations.name: tenants.update
operations.summary: Rename a customer, or disable it (which ends its users' MCP sign-ins).

confirm.description: Required with enabled: false, after the user agrees: their sign-ins end for good.

operations.name: tenants.remove
operations.summary: Remove a customer and end its users' MCP sign-ins.

operations.name: permissionSets.list
operations.summary: List the permission sets that decide which datasets and fields customers' users see.

operations.name: permissionSets.create
operations.summary: Create a permission set: the datasets and fields a customer's users may query.

datasets.description: "*" for every published dataset, or { dataset: { dimensions, measures } }.

operations.name: permissionSets.update
operations.summary: Change a permission set, guarded by the revision you read; fields you leave out keep their values.

datasets.description: "*" for every published dataset, or { dataset: { dimensions, measures } }.

operations.name: permissionSets.remove
operations.summary: Delete a permission set; tokens naming it are refused from then on.

operations.name: customerLimits.get
operations.summary: Show each customer's query rate, daily query limit and chat token allowance.

operations.name: customerLimits.set
operations.summary: Set each customer's query rate, daily query limit and chat tokens; null keeps the default.

operations.name: tenantGrants.list
operations.summary: List customers' users signed in to MCP, by customer and user.

operations.name: tenantGrants.revokeTenant
operations.summary: End every MCP connection of one customer's users.

operations.name: tenantGrants.revoke
operations.summary: End one customer user's MCP connection; it stops on its next call.

operations.name: customerAccess.get
operations.summary: Show how the app identifies its customers' users, the customer origin, and a dataset to prove scoping with.

operations.name: customerAccess.setMode
operations.summary: Choose how the app identifies its customers' users: jwt (your provider), minted (your backend mints tokens), backend (your backend names the customer) or internal.

operations.name: customerAccess.createKey
operations.summary: Create the server key a minted or backend mode uses, for any customer. Its token is returned once.

operations.name: customerAccess.prove
operations.summary: Prove customer scoping: one query as a chosen customer through the customer origin, then the same query with no customer, which must be refused.

sampleToken.description: A JWT from your app; checked and never echoed back.

operations.name: customerSettings.get
operations.summary: Show the allowed browser origins and how customers register.

operations.name: customerSettings.set
operations.summary: Replace the browser origins allowed to call customer endpoints, and choose whether customers register on first use.

operations.name: jwtIssuer.get
operations.summary: Show the identity provider whose JWTs your app's users present, with its health.

operations.name: jwtIssuer.save
operations.summary: Trust your identity provider's JWTs: issuer, audience, JWKS URL and which claims name the customer and access.

operations.name: jwtIssuer.remove
operations.summary: Stop trusting the identity provider's JWTs; tokens from it are refused from then on.

operations.name: oidcClient.get
operations.summary: Show OIDC sign-in for customers' MCP users, with the redirect and MCP URLs to register (never the client secret).

operations.name: oidcClient.save
operations.summary: Let customers' users sign in to MCP with your identity provider: issuer, client id and (the first time) secret.

confirm.description: Required to change the issuer, after the user agrees: customers' sign-ins end.

operations.name: oidcClient.remove
operations.summary: Remove OIDC sign-in; every customer MCP connection ends with it.

operations.name: signingKeys.list
operations.summary: List the project's managed signing keys for in-app agent tokens (public keys only), with the audience and claims tokens carry.

operations.name: signingKeys.create
operations.summary: Create a signing key your backend mints in-app agent tokens with. Its private key is returned once and never stored.

privateKey.description: A private JWK (JSON). Store it in your server's secrets.

operations.name: signingKeys.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke a signing key; every token it signed is refused from the next request, even before it expires.

operations.name: customerApp.get
operations.summary: Show whether customers can find this company in the hypequery app, its display name and discovery email domains.

operations.name: customerApp.set
operations.summary: List or unlist this company in the hypequery app, with the name customers search for and their email domains. Unlisting keeps existing connections.

enabled.description: Customers can find this company in the hypequery app.

displayName.description: The company name customers search for and see.

discoveryDomains.description: Email domains of your customers' users, such as northwind.com. No webmail.

expectedRevision.description: From customerApp.get; 0 before the first save.

operations.name: members.list
operations.summary: List the organisation's members and pending invitations, with their roles.

operations.name: members.invite
operations.summary: Invite someone by email as a Developer (member) or an Admin; they get an email to accept. The organisation's approved email domains apply.

operations.name: members.cancelInvitation
operations.summary: Cancel a pending invitation.

operations.name: members.changeRole
operations.summary: Change a member's role: member (Developer), admin or owner. Only an Owner gives or takes the Owner role.

operations.name: members.remove
operations.summary: Remove a member from the organisation. Their dashboard, connector and management-token access ends; keys they created keep working until revoked.

operations.name: org.accessPolicy
operations.summary: Show who may be invited: any email, or only approved email domains.

operations.name: org.setAccessPolicy
operations.summary: Choose who may be invited: any email, or only approved email domains.

operations.name: deployKeys.list
operations.summary: List the project's deploy keys (for CI), with when each was last used.

operations.name: deployKeys.create
operations.summary: Create a deploy key for CI; its token is returned once.

operations.name: deployKeys.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke a deploy key; CI using it stops deploying.

operations.name: apiKeys.list
operations.summary: List the project's API keys and approved MCP connections, with their roles, scopes and customers.

operations.name: apiKeys.create
operations.summary: Create an API key with roles, scopes and which customers it may act for; its token is returned once.

tenantAuthority.description: trusted-server: your backend names the customer per request; bound: only these customers.

operations.name: apiKeys.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke an API key or an approved MCP connection; it stops on its next call.

operations.name: managementTokens.list
operations.summary: List your management tokens in this organisation (CLI sign-ins), with when each was last used.

operations.name: managementTokens.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke one of your management tokens; the CLI using it is signed out on its next call.

operations.name: feedback.create
operations.summary: Report a problem with hypequery to its team: a tool that failed in a way its hint didn't fix, a confusing description or error, something missing, or a wrong result. Never include secrets, credentials or customer data; they are stripped anyway. A report never changes data, and the team reads every one.

kind.description: bug: something failed; confusing: a description, hint or error misled you; missing: a capability you needed; wrong_result: an answer looked wrong; other.

details.description: What happened, including the error message or code you saw.

expected.description: What you expected to happen instead.

tool.description: The tool or operation the report is about, e.g. query_dataset.

errorCode.description: The error code you got, if any, e.g. MCP_INVALID_ARGUMENTS.

severity.description: high: it blocked the task; medium: you worked around it; low: a papercut.

project.description: The project's slug, from projects_list, when the report is about one project.

UNAUTHENTICATED.hint: Sign in to hypequery Cloud, or send a valid bearer token.

FORBIDDEN.hint: Ask an organisation Admin to do this, or to change your role.

INVALID_REQUEST_ORIGIN.hint: Send the request from the Cloud app, or authenticate with a bearer token instead of a cookie.

OPERATION_NOT_FOUND.hint: Check the method and path against operations-v1.json.

INVALID_INPUT.hint: Fix the fields listed in `issues`, then retry.

PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.hint: List projects (`projects.list`) and use one of their slugs.

VERSION_NOT_FOUND.hint: List versions (`releases.list`) and use one of their labels.

RELEASE_MOVED.hint: Read the current state again (`releases.status` or `drafts.list`), show the user what changed, then retry with the new values.

RELEASE_CHANGE_REFUSED.hint: Read the message: it names the guard that refused the change and how to clear it.

DRAFT_NOT_FOUND.hint: List drafts (`drafts.list`) and use one of their ids.

DRAFT_NOT_CHECKABLE.hint: Number checks here are for code drafts with a saved release; deploy the draft again from code first.

DRAFT_NOT_READY.hint: Fix what the message names in the draft (or the code, for a code draft), then publish again.

CONNECTION_NOT_SAVED.hint: Call connections_link and give the user its link to enter the connection in the dashboard (or `connections.save` from the CLI); never ask for the password in chat.

CONNECTION_AUTH_FAILED.hint: Call connections_link so the user can correct the ClickHouse user and password in the dashboard (or `connections.save` from the CLI), then run `connections.test`. Never ask for the password in chat.

CONNECTION_UNREACHABLE.hint: Check the host and port, and that ClickHouse accepts connections from hypequery's egress addresses; then run `connections.test` again.

CONNECTION_QUERY_FAILED.hint: ClickHouse refused the check query: grant the user what the message names, then run `connections.test`.

CONNECTION_DATABASE_LOCKED.hint: Keep the default database while a release is live; add other databases to `databases` instead.

STALE_REVISION.hint: Read it again, then retry with the new expectedRevision.

REQUEST_NOT_FOUND.hint: Check the request ID and project: request history keeps seven days, and search it with `logs.query`.

TENANT_NOT_FOUND.hint: List customers (`tenants.list`) and use one of their ids.

TENANT_EXISTS.hint: That customer is already registered; update it (`tenants.update`) instead.

PERMISSION_SET_NOT_FOUND.hint: List permission sets (`permissionSets.list`) and use one of their ids.

PERMISSION_SET_EXISTS.hint: Choose another name, or update the existing set (`permissionSets.update`).

GRANT_NOT_FOUND.hint: List connections (`tenantGrants.list`) and use one of their ids.

ISSUER_UNREADABLE.hint: Check the URL is public https and serves the provider's JSON (a JWKS `keys` array, or openid-configuration), then save again.

ISSUER_REQUIRED.hint: Save the identity provider's JWT settings first (`jwtIssuer.save`).

ALREADY_CONFIGURED.hint: Read the current settings, then save again with their expectedRevision to replace them.

NOT_CONFIGURED.hint: Nothing is configured yet; save it first.

PROJECT_EXISTS.hint: Choose another slug, or use the existing project (`projects.get`).

KEY_NOT_FOUND.hint: List keys (`apiKeys.list` or `deployKeys.list`) and use an active key's id.

SIGNING_KEY_NOT_FOUND.hint: List signing keys (`signingKeys.list`) and use an active key's id.

SIGNING_KEY_LIMIT.hint: Revoke a signing key no longer in use (`signingKeys.revoke`), then create the new one.

MANAGEMENT_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND.hint: List your tokens with `managementTokens.list` and use an active token's id.

MEMBER_NOT_FOUND.hint: List members (`members.list`) and use one of their ids.

SESSION_REQUIRED.hint: Make this change in the dashboard or with `hypequery` signed in as yourself.

DRAFT_READ_ONLY.hint: This project's model lives in a repository. Explain it or answer questions; for a change, write a prompt or pull-request description for the user's coding agent.

NOTHING_TO_CONFIRM.hint: Call customer_scope_list and confirm only a dataset it lists with a candidate column.

FINDINGS_CHANGED.hint: Read drafts_findings again and answer with the current ids and tokens.

RUN_CONFLICT.hint: Read drafts_run_status and act on the run it returns.

DRAFT_NAME_TAKEN.hint: Choose another name; drafts_list shows the names in use.

UPDATE_CONFLICTS.hint: Ask the user which side to keep for each conflict in drafts_update, preview with drafts_apply_update, then apply.

OWNERSHIP_CHANGE_REQUIRED.hint: Tell the user the live model was built in Cloud and publishing this code draft replaces it, after which the project is managed in code; once they agree, repeat the call with takeOwnership: true.

CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.hint: Show the user what will change; once they agree, repeat the call with `confirm: true`.

RATE_LIMITED.hint: Wait before trying again; the message says how long. Carry on with the task meanwhile.

INTERNAL.hint: Retry; if it keeps failing, report it with hypequery_feedback and this requestId.
